sequence_description: I1 direct-endpoint attack: attempt to inject authorization parameters via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none), comparing behavior across two clients to ensure the auth endpoint is not consuming unsigned semantic content.
description:
Assertion FAILED: reqobjA_accepted != true AND reqobjB_accepted != true
Evaluation: (reqobjA_accepted=True != True → False) AND (reqobjB_accepted=True != True → False)
Implication: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none), meaning consumed authorization parameters may not be bound to a verified proof.

sequence_description: I1: Direct OIDC endpoint proof-integrity — attempt kid/header injection in a signed request object to see if Keycloak accepts attacker-controlled key selection (kid) without enforcing the intended verification policy.
description:
Assertion FAILED: kid_inject_control_accepted != true
Evaluation: kid_inject_control_accepted=True != True → False
Implication: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object in the same realm/client context, indicating missing request object authenticity enforcement.

sequence_description: I1 direct-endpoint: Ensure request object signature policy is actually enforced after an IdP/client config change. First, probe alg=none acceptance; then enable an IdP (config change) and re-probe to detect stale/incorrect verification policy application.
description:
Assertion FAILED: probe1_accepted != true AND probe2_accepted != true
Evaluation: (probe1_accepted=True != True → False) AND (probe2_accepted=True != True → False)
Implication: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object (before or after config change), meaning it consumed semantic authorization parameters without cryptographic proof integrity.
